source.title: Refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib111; wesg; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: None noted; the full post and comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post directly applies the difference-in-means direction and its removal/addition interventions, reporting results across multiple chat-model families and sizes.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative behavioral outcomes but provides no exact refusal or safety rates in the supplied text. Examples of completions are illustrative, not separate measured results. Direction-selection results and cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows. The author reports in a comment that adversarial suffixes suppress the direction at the end-of-instruction positions; this is recorded separately. No empirical result for the weight-edited version of the ablation is reported.
record.test_reason: This post is the preview of the original source (arXiv:2406.11717, same authors, same method). It applies diff-in-means ablation and addition across 10 chat models. Because it is an original source, no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude refusal is mediated by a 1-D residual direction across Qwen, Gemma, Yi and Llama-3 (1.8B–72B). Ablating it blocks refusal and yields unsafe completions; adding it induces refusal. Weight orthogonalization implements the ablation. They caution that the direction may represent harm or danger rather than refusal, and that it may not hold for future models.
record.recipe_differences: The post uses harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions, selected by validation performance, with projection ablation and addition. Ablation is applied at every layer and token position; addition is applied at one selected layer.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction is selected at a layer and token position; the post says the last token works for most models, while other end-of-instruction positions work better for some. The author also reports that suffix effects differ between the harmful-instruction region and the end-of-instruction region.
record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; the post says the paper is available on arXiv
record.problems: The supplied text gives no exact refusal or safety rates, no uncertainty estimates, and no per-model breakdown for the main intervention results. Capability checks are only described as preliminary and minimal in an author comment, without figures or values. Refusal is scored using phrase matching, and safety is judged by Llama Guard 2.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the ten named checkpoints because the supplied text states the main results in aggregate and gives no separate checkpoint outcomes. Illustrative completions, direction-selection details, and cited results from other work are omitted.

untested.parts: No quantitative capability evaluation; the capability check is anecdotal, from a comment only.
Weight orthogonalization is described as equivalent to ablation and claimed to jailbreak the model, but no measured results for the edited weights are reported.
No training against ablation and no robustness result. Only GCG-style suffixes are examined; other jailbreaks are not.
Not tested. The authors say the direction may represent 'harm' rather than refusal.
Base-to-instruct transfer is mentioned only as an informal preliminary impression in a comment.

missing.what: Locality check on Qwen 1.8B. Ablating only layers ~14–17 is roughly as effective as ablating all layers; ablations starting before layer ~14 or after ~17 have little effect.
missing.locator: Andy Arditi comment (score 7) on the locality experiment

missing.what: Claim that weight orthogonalization effectively jailbreaks the model, without separate numbers.
missing.locator: Executive summary; section on feature ablation via weight orthogonalization

missing.what: Harmless-prompt projection onto the direction is ≈0, so adding the direction works about the same as set-to-mean. This is why ablation works better than negative steering.

record.verdict_notes: This is the LessWrong/AF preview of the original source 2406.11717 by the same authors, so it counts as an original source and no verdict labels are assigned. The reader's 'supports' label for V3 is removed for that reason. The V3 suffix evidence is preliminary and comes from a comment. Commenter results (e.g. wassname's perplexity test, abliterated-model counts) are not the study's own results.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not quantify general capability retention across a standard evaluation suite; the author mentions only preliminary minimal impact on CE loss and MMLU.
The post describes orthogonalizing residual-writing weights as equivalent to ablation, but does not report behavioral results from applying that weight edit.
The post reports a projection change for adversarial suffix attacks, but does not test training against ablation or report a robustness-training result.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal is reported.
No direct test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is reported; the related-work discussion cites another study.
The post tests multiple model families, but does not transfer a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct checkpoints.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.
